To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we developed a new code to trace subhaloes, hbt, that is able to well trace the evolutionary history for a large number of subhaloes in a large volume of simulation box, especially for those in high-density environment.

we develop a new code that is able to find the full subhalo catalogue of dark matter halos and keep a full record on the merger history of the subhaloes; this code is able to find subhaloes that are missed by other popular codes; we show the importance of rebinding of stripped subhalo mass and local accretion of the background mass; we provide a detailed comparison of different subhalo finding codes and show that hBT is the best code in terms

(i) hbt is one of the most successful codes in finding subhaloes and tracing their evolutionary histories; (ii) hbt allows subhaloes to grow through local mass accretion, hence allowing mergings of satellite subhalos, and rebinding of stripped subhalos, which is important in high-density regions; (iii) hbt can be applied to any N-body simulations with any mass resolutions
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the evolution of dark matter subhalos.
the study of the evolution of substructures in dark matter haloes in the framework of the hierarchical clustering scenario.
the development and application of an efficient code, hbt, to trace the merger histories of dark matter subhalos in N-body simulations.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
hbt is a powerful and robust tool for subhalo finding and tracking in cosmological simulations.
hbt is a robust and reliable subhalo finder that can trace the complete merger histories of subhaloes, especially those that are difficult to be resolved by other codes.
hbt is a robust, efficient and accurate code that can be used to find and trace the evolutionary history for dark matter subhalo in simulations.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the hbt code can be used to study subhalo populations with a high degree of completeness and accuracy.
hbt provides a reliable tool for tracing subhaloes’ life histories in simulations.
we have developed a new code, hbt, to find subhaloes in N-body simulation, and have demonstrated its success by comparing to the recent benchmark test of subhalo finding.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the subhalo population in simulations is very sensitive to the details of the unbinding algorithm and the treatment of rebinding.
subhalo evolution in a cosmological setting is a highly non-trivial process that requires careful treatment of the physics involved, which is not always reflected by other subhalo findings.

the subhalo catalogue can be obtained by a careful and physical tracking of the merger history of haloes and that the subhaloes’ mass is a function of time, and not a constant as is usually assumed in the literature.
